{"output":"No"}

**Reasoning:**

- `k = 20`
- `s = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcdefg"` (n=33), so `s[i] = chr(97 + i mod 26)`
- `t = "gfedcbazyxwvutsrqponmlkjihgfedcba"` (m=33), so `t[j] = chr(97 + (6-j) mod 26)`

The program computes the standard Levenshtein edit distance.

**Match analysis:** `s[i] == t[j]` iff `i ≡ 6 - j (mod 26)`, i.e., `i + j ≡ 6 (mod 26)`. Since `i + j` ranges over `[0, 64]`, matches occur only on anti-diagonals `i+j = 6, 32, 58`.

Within one anti-diagonal, increasing `i` forces decreasing `j`, so any common subsequence (chain of matches increasing in both coordinates) contains **at most 1 match per anti-diagonal** → LCS ≤ 3 (e.g., `d@(3,3)`, `q@(16,16)`, `d@(29,29)` — the identity alignment already achieves 3 matches: i = 3, 16, 29 since `2i ≡ 6 mod 26`).

**Edit distance bound:** With unit-cost insert/delete/substitute, cost = `(33−p) + (33−p) + subs = 66 − 2p + subs = 66 − (p + matches)`. Since `p ≤ 33` and `matches ≤ 3`, cost ≥ `66 − 36 = 30`, achieved by the identity alignment (30 substitutions). So edit distance = **30 > 20** → output `No`.
